Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

everything pronoun

also all things, everything else

classical

Cic. Fam. 16.4.4: omnia dēpōne
Cic. Sen. 21: omnia quae cūrant meminērunt

omnia, omnium n. pl.

adjective used as a noun (neuter plural of omnis)

everything, all things

Latin says “all things”, in the plural: ut sint omnia parāta, have everything ready (Cic. Fam. 14.20.1). “Everything else” is cētera.

Other words

  • cūncta, cūnctōrum n. pl. — everything, all together

    adjective used as a noun · also used · classical · Ov. Met. 15.177–178: nihil est tōtō, quod perstet, in orbe. cūncta fluunt

    Lewis & Short: all in a body, all together, the whole.

  • cētera, cēterōrum n. pl. — everything else, the rest

    adjective used as a noun · also used · classical · Liv. 1.9.3: ut cētera

Examples

  • in Tusculānum nōs ventūrōs putāmus aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē. ibi ut sint omnia parāta

    we expect to reach Tusculum on the Nones or the day after. Have everything ready thereCic. Fam. 14.20.1

  • omnia dēpōne, corporī servī

    drop everything and look after your healthCic. Fam. 16.4.4

  • omnia quae cūrant meminērunt

    they remember everything they care aboutCic. Sen. 21

See also is everything all right?, something, all gone.
